transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 16:00 PT
Duration: approx 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Veridian CTO), Dana Liu (Veridian ML Platform Lead), Samir Patel (Veridian SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, welcome back for the weekly sync, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — hit-rate review, outlier cohort, eviction ideas, next steps. priya will walk the numbers first.
[00:23] Priya: yep, hi all. i'm sharing the dashboard link in chat — the summary: overall KV hit-rate ticked up from ~18% to ~26% this week after the prompt-normalization we pushed, prefix hit-rate stayed flatter, from about 12% to 14%. i want to call out a specific cohort (c cohort in your workspace) that's dragging prefix reuse down.
[00:45] Alex: sorry can you repeat the cohort name? c-cohort? we had several segs.
[00:51] Priya: yeah, sorry, it's the "clinical-chat-bot" cohort — high variance in user phrasing, lots of paraphrase. their prefix lengths are short which reduces exact prefix matches.
[01:07] Dana: that makes sense — our UX team pushed a quick question-normalizer that truncates context, so the prefix is often only two to three tokens, which obviously is low reuse.
[01:21] Samir: also, network wise we've had some transient timeouts; wondering if that skews the metrics because requests fall back to cold path which we then double count.
[01:33] Jordan: good call. priya, do we instrument fallback counts in the export?
[01:37] Priya: yes — the CSV i dropped has columns for fallback_count, kv_hit, prefix_hit, seq_len, model_variant, and route. but fwiw the automatic fallback label sometimes transcribes as "fall back" in the logs so watch that.
[01:51] Alex: cool. can you run through the high-level delta again — what's the real token savings? we're trying to quantify cost impact.
[01:59] Priya: on average, moving KV from 18% to 26% saved ~11% token consumption on generation for the mixed clinical workload. that maps to roughly 9% per-token cost reduction assuming same model/cost profile. prefix-only savings are smaller — about 3-4% since your prefix lengths are short. combined strategy nets about 12-13% in practice.
[02:23] Dana: okay, that aligns with our back-of-envelope. but when you say "prefix-only" did you mean exact-match prefix or fuzzy prefix?
[02:33] Priya: right now it's exact-match prefix; we discussed fuzzy-prefix in the previous call but haven't enabled it and it has edge cases with KV indexing. fuzzy helps paraphrase but costs more in lookups, could raise latency.
[02:46] Jordan: which leads to eviction policies — we saw a couple of spikes in the eviction log where many short prefixes pushed out mid-day. priya, show the eviction chart.
[02:55] Priya: sharing. primary observation: LRU policy is evicting longer-lived high-value keys because a surge of ephemeral short prefixes from that clinical-cohort floods the cache during morning shift. TTL-based with score (score = hits * token_savings) would protect high-value keys.
[03:15] Alex: so TTL+score would mean we keep some keys longer even if they aren't recently used? that's good for our frequently referenced guidelines.
[03:24] Priya: exactly. we also proposed a small per-cohort reservation — e.g., 10% of KV capacity reserved for clinical cohort to avoid them thrashing others. that reduced cross-cohort eviction in simulation by ~22%.
[03:37] Dana: reservation sounds promising but is that something we can tune dynamically, or would it be a static config?
[03:43] Priya: currently static in the POC config, but we can iterate to make it adaptive — track eviction rates per cohort and auto-adjust reservation monthly. that's roadmap-level but doable.
[03:56] Samir: are there any security implications with cohort reservations? e.g., does that require new RBAC or logging changes?
[04:03] Jordan: good question. no extra RBAC just for reservation, it's an internal routing config. it does increase audit surface in the sense you'd want those metrics in your audit logs. priya, we can expose cohort eviction events to the audit stream.
[04:16] Priya: yep we can add eviction events and cohort tags to the existing audit log payload (timestamp, key_id, reason). note: the log payload size bump may affect retention costs.
[04:29] Alex: can you clarify the retention window? we need at least 90 days for compliance.
[04:34] Priya: retention at the moment is configurable; default for POC is 30 days. enterprise tier supports 90+ and can push to your SIEM or S3. we'll include the log retention config in the security doc we send.
[04:46] Dana: perfect. on the prefix reuse front, any low-effort tricks? we were thinking of canonicalizing some prompts at the app layer.
[04:55] Jordan: yes — prompt normalization at the client side gave us the bump this week. specifics: lowercase, remove polite tokens, collapse date stamps; that moved several low-frequency variants into a canonical prefix, which increased exact-match rates.
[05:10] Dana: interesting — our concern is losing semantic nuance if we normalize too aggressively for clinical text.
[05:17] Priya: correct. you should control normalization rules — we recommend safe-normalize config where we avoid removing punctuation used in ICD codes and preserve units. we'll share a recommended rule set.
[05:30] Alex: there's also mention earlier about batch sizing. can you summarize tradeoffs? our latency SLO is 250ms p99 for interactive flows.
[05:38] Priya: batching increases throughput and reduces unit cost but increases tail latency. in our tests, going from batch size 1 to 8 improved throughput by ~2.8x but p99 latency went from ~180ms to ~360ms on the same hardware. Our runtime supports dynamic batching with latency caps so you can prioritize latency SLOs.
[05:58] Jordan: note we can set a latency cap so batches flush at, say, 120ms to respect your p99 target — that'll reduce batching benefit but keep you within SLO.
[06:08] Samir: that flush timer, is it per-model or per-route? we have different routes for triage vs. documentation.
[06:14] Priya: per-route — you can set different batching caps per API route. practically we recommend stricter caps for interactive triage flows and looser caps for background summarization.
[06:25] Dana: back to the outlier cohort: what's our A/B plan?
[06:29] Priya: propose A = current LRU + prefix exact-match (control), B = TTL+score for eviction + 10% cohort reservation + prompt-normalization at app layer. run for 3 days on randomized 25% of traffic from that cohort. metrics: prefix_hit, kv_hit, percent_requests_falling_back_to_cold, median_latency, cost-per-1k-requests.
[06:50] Alex: 3 days OK. can we do 1k requests sample first to sanity check?
[06:55] Priya: absolutely. dana, can you seed 1k randomized requests from last week's logs and run them through the staging route?
[07:03] Dana: yes, we can do that. i'll run it and upload results by tuesday.
[07:08] Jordan: perfect. quick question — Priya earlier mentioned fuzzy prefix; in what scenario should we enable that?
[07:15] Priya: fuzzy is useful when paraphrase is high — like freeform patient questions. it maps semantically-similar prefixes using a small embedding index; hit-rate increases but lookup latency grows ~10-20ms depending on index size. we can make it hybrid: fuzzy for long prefixes > 8 tokens only.
[07:33] Samir: that 10-20ms extra might push our p99 over limit for triage; but if we gate fuzzy to long prefixes and background flows, could be ok.
[07:41] Jordan: agreed. gate fuzzy by route and prefix length. we'll add that to config suggestions.
[07:48] Alex: any anomalies in model variant routing? some of our traffic is routed to a smaller quantized model and that could affect cache keys.
[07:56] Priya: yes, model_variant is a separate namespace for cache keys — keys are namespaced by model and quantization profile. your mixed routing to quantized model explains why some keys miss when the same semantic prompt hit on non-quantized variant. we can either unify keys across model variants (with caveats) or warm both caches.
[08:14] Dana: what's the recommended approach? unified keys sound risky if output differs.
[08:19] Priya: recommended: warm both caches for high-value prompts; unify only when output parity is validated. for the POC, warming both is simpler.
[08:29] Alex: ok. on compliance: SSO and audit log export — are we good with our standard enterprise connector for SAML?
[08:36] Jordan: yes, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. audit exports can be pushed to your S3 bucket with encryption via your KMS. we'll include the deployment steps in the security doc.
[08:48] Samir: please note we need KMS ARN and our engs will verify policies. we'll send that in a separate email.
[08:54] Jordan: perfect. quick pause — any other pressing blockers?
[09:00] Alex: only one — we saw a tail latency measurement that looked off: p999 spikes near 2s during morning surge. can we investigate whether that's due to cache misses or network?
[09:10] Priya: we looked at the initial traces; 60% of p999 events correlated with cold starts on a particular node group that had scheduled maintenance. seems like a provisioning artifact. we can instrument a per-node cold-start flag and exclude maintenance windows in the POC metrics.
[09:27] Dana: was that the group with the recent kernel bump?
[09:29] Priya: yes. Samir, the node metadata you sent showed that bump coincided with the morning window.
[09:35] Samir: right — we ran a kernel update but thought it was rolling-safe. i'll coordinate to avoid rolling during peak.
[09:40] Jordan: good. i'll add note in the runbook to freeze infra changes during bench windows.
[09:45] Priya: back to metrics: i uploaded a CSV with per-request rows and we recommend you look at "seq_len" vs prefix_hits scatter. there's a visible elbow at seq_len 6 where prefix hit rapidly drops. that's a useful threshold for gating fuzzy prefix.
[10:03] Dana: interesting — so rule could be: if seq_len >= 6 use fuzzy, else exact-match.
[10:09] Priya: yes and only for non-critical triage routes unless you accept higher tail latency.
[10:15] Alex: does the POC runtime support that gating today?
[10:18] Priya: yes — per-route and per-prefix-length gating is supported via our routing config. i'll paste the sample YAML in the follow-up.
[10:26] Samir: any suggestions on how we should surface these cache metrics into Grafana on our side?
[10:31] Jordan: we can push a Prometheus export with per-route metrics and cohort labels. suggested dashboards: kv_hit_rate, prefix_hit_rate, eviction_rate, fallback_count, p50/p95/p99 latency per route.
[10:43] Dana: we have that stack so prometheus -> grafana is easiest. please include metric names and label keys in the doc.
[10:50] Priya: will do. also including an example alert rule for eviction_rate > 0.05 for a sustained 10m window.
[10:58] Alex: are we tracking cost deltas per config change? we'd like weekly rollups.
[11:03] Priya: Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns per model/route. for POC we can enable a weekly export to your S3. the cost delta estimate we gave earlier (9%) is modeled assuming steady mix; we'll provide a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet.
[11:17] Jordan: ok let's shift to concrete next steps recap.
[11:21] Priya: recap: 1) Redwood sends KV/prefix hit-rate export and eviction-policy variants (Jordan/Priya) 2) Veridian runs 1k randomized request sanity test and full 3-day A/B for clinical cohort (Dana) 3) Veridian provides network egress and KMS arn (Samir) 4) schedule in-lab latency bench (Jordan to propose dates).
[11:40] Alex: that's right. can we get the export today?
[11:43] Priya: yes i dropped the raw CSV but i'll send a cleaned drilldown by tomorrow.
[11:47] Dana: i'll start the 1k today and aim to upload by tuesday.
[11:51] Samir: i'll pull KMS details and send to Jordan by friday.
[11:55] Jordan: cool. any other questions from anyone?
[11:58] Alex: not from me. thanks, team.
[12:01] Jordan: thanks all, see you next week.

--- End transcript ---

Notes: transcript contains typical autocomplete errors: "K-V cash" mis-heard in one block, "fall back" vs "fallback" label variations. References to config artifacts: link to dashboard and CSV (shared in chat), sample routing YAML to be attached in follow-up email.
